text: The Safety of Melasma Treatment in Vitiligo Patients: An International E-Delphi Study. Vitiligo and melasma frequently coexist, creating a treatment dilemma, since agents effective for one condition can destabilize the other, and no consensus currently exists on safe management. We conducted a scoping literature review (through June 2023) on treatment of patients with concomitant vitiligo and melasma, followed by a two-round international e-Delphi survey (22 experts from 14 countries; consensus defined as ≥ 70% agreement) and a final online consensus meeting. Only one study supported the safe use of oral tranexamic acid for melasma in vitiligo patients. Expert consensus favored prioritizing vitiligo treatment, particularly when active, while incorporating patient's preferences. Targeted phototherapy is suitable for localized facial lesions of vitiligo, and non-facial vitiligo can be treated alongside melasma after covering the face. Topical calcineurin inhibitors, ruxolitinib, tretinoin, corticosteroids, and oral tranexamic acid can be used. Lasers and chemical peels were recommended only with caution by experienced pigment specialists. Until there is enough scientific evidence, hydroquinone would be replaced by other safer cosmetic lightening agents (e.g., niacinamide, ascorbic acid, thiamidol, melasyl), which show comparable efficacy with less theoretical risk. This first international consensus offers practical, patient-centered guidance for managing coexisting vitiligo and melasma, emphasizing individualized, disease-activity-based treatment sequencing. Trial Registration: PROSPERO reference number: RD42023395586 Significance. Depigmenting agents used for melasma inhibit melanogenesis, a mechanism that can further compromise the already-stressed melanocyte populations characteristic of vitiligo. This consensus gives clinicians an expert-informed pathway through a common but understudied comorbidity. It also identifies a clear research gap: controlled, mechanistic comparisons of hydroquinone against newer tyrosinase inhibitors specifically in vitiligo-prone skin are still lacking.

C3 Glomerulopathy in Autoinflammatory-Pancytopenia Syndrome: A Case Report. Autoinflammatory-pancytopenia syndrome (AIPCS) is a rare autosomal recessive disease caused by a mutation in the deoxyribonuclease II (DNASE2) gene. It has mainly haematological manifestations and recurrent fevers. The kidney could be involved in the form of proteinuria, membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis (MPGN) or immune complex deposition rather than acute kidney injury (AKI) or C3 glomerulopathy (C3G). A six-year-old male child presented with high-grade fever, AKI, generalized edema and hypertension. He had a history of recurrent hospital admission with fever, arthritis, skin rash and recurrent infections in the form of diarrhoea and chest infection. He had stunted growth, pallor, hepatosplenomegaly (HSM) and skin hyperpigmentation at the sites of the healed vasculitic skin rash. He was diagnosed with hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis and received its protocol of treatment with improvement of fever. However, pancytopenia and HSM were still progressive. Laboratory investigations revealed pancytopenia, impaired kidney function tests and heavy-range proteinuria with persistent low C3 level. Kidney biopsy revealed C3 deposition suggestive of C3G, with 20% global glomerulosclerosis, mild interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (10%). Kidney function tests normalized after receiving intravenous methylprednisolone, but proteinuria is still persistent, which indicates that AKI was on top of chronic kidney disease in the presence of C3G. Whole exome sequencing revealed a homozygous (missense) variant of uncertain significance with pathogenic evidence in exon-6 of the DNASE2 gene causing AIPCS. In conclusion, C3G is a new form of kidney involvement associated with AIPCS. Kidney histopathology should be combined with phenotypic-genotypic aspects of AIPCS.

Age and disease status as negative prognostic factors for 5-year survival in chondrosarcoma: A single-institution analysis. While Western literature identifies age, histological grade, tumor characteristics, and metastasis as key prognostic factors for chondrosarcoma survival, data specifically focusing on the Taiwanese population remain sparse.
